subject: Quant/batching credit split & operational handoff for Velocity.ai pilot
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@velocity.ai>
Cc: Priya Nambiar <priya@velocity.ai>
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot proposal + ask: quant / batching / credit split

Hi Ravi / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — really appreciated the clarity on your realtime use case. Attached is a short pilot proposal that frames a 3-month evaluation: workload profile, success metrics (95th perc P95 tail latency < 300ms for 512-token context), and a proposed credit structure to get you live quickly.

Ask: could your infra/ML team confirm any hard latency SLOs and peak qps? That will help us set sensible batching thresholds and whether to recommend more aggressive quantization.

Commercial framing (initial): 50k USD in pilot credits spread over 3 months (we suggested 30% upfront, 70% consumption-based). We’re open to splitting the credits differently if you need more upfront runway.

Attachments: pilot_proposal.pdf (pdf)

Next steps: if you’re comfortable, I can loop in Camila (solutions/ops) for a quick go/no-go on recommended quant profiles and an ops handoff checklist.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ravi Shah <ravi@velocity.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Nambiar <priya@velocity.ai>
Date: 2027-12-02T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal + ask: quant / batching / credit split

Aditya — thanks for the proposal. A few clarifications from our side: we’re targeting conversational search with ~3M tokens/month in month 1, scaling to ~10M tokens/month by month 3. P95 latency target for 512 tokens is 250ms end-to-end (including network).

Questions:
- Which quant profile would preserve accuracy for our reranker + long-context prompts?
- Are there recommended batching window/size defaults for low tail latency at modest qps (~8–12 req/s)?
- We prefer credits that cover the first 6–8 weeks of dev/validation, so a bit more upfront would be helpful.

Happy to set a short tech call with your solutions team.

—Ravi
Ravi Shah | Head of ML | Velocity.ai
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@velocity.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Nambiar <priya@velocity.ai>
Date: 2027-12-03T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal + ask: quant / batching / credit split

Hi Ravi — looping in answers from the infra/solutions side (quick summary, happy to go deeper on a call):

Technical recommendations (short):
- Quantization: start with dynamic INT8 (per-channel) for your base model if you can tolerate ~0.5–1% eval delta on reranking metrics. For more aggressive cost reduction, we recommend the \"redwood-1.5q\" 4-bit aware quant variant but reserve that for a second-phase validation (A/B on eval set). See attached notes (quant_profile_notes.md).
- Batching: for your QPS (8–12 req/s) and 250ms P95 target, aim for a batching window of 10–20ms and max batch size 8–12. Continuous batching with an adaptive filler works well; set hard tail-latency caps to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Caching: implement prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and frequent user intents. We suggest keeping a small LRU cache per model shard (config: 1–2k entries) to capture the majority of repeated prefixes.
- Model variant: use the higher-throughput \"redwood-optim-1.5q\" variant for production once the eval delta is validated. In the pilot, run both standard and optim variants on a sample split to quantify quality vs token-cost.

Commercial suggestion (ops-friendly):
- Credit split: 40% upfront pilot credit to cover development and validation, 60% consumption credits applied through month 3. If you sign a 12-month commitment after pilot, apply a further 25% conversion bonus to the remaining usage-based credits.
- Operational handoff: we can provide a 2-day remote onboarding (ops + infra) and a one-week tuning window to adjust batching thresholds.

Attachments: quant_profile_notes.md (markdown) — details on expected eval deltas and safe thresholds.

If the commercial framing above looks reasonable, Aditya can convert this to an MAP and we’ll schedule a short ops kickoff.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@velocity.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Priya Nambiar <priya@velocity.ai>
Date: 2027-12-05T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal + ask: quant / batching / credit split

Ravi — thanks Camila, that level of detail is perfect.

Commercial counter-proposal from our side to reflect your ask for more upfront runway:
- 30% upfront pilot credit paid at kickoff (applies to the 50k USD pilot pool).
- An additional 20% pilot credit we’ll milestone-release after completion of the first week of integration (basic infra checks + a short quality evaluation on your sample).
- If Velocity signs a 12-month renewal within 30 days post-pilot, we’ll convert up to 50% of unused pilot credits into committed-credit at a 15% bonus.

I’ve updated the mutual action plan draft: https://app.redwood.com/docs/mutual-action-plan — I can send a DocuSign when you confirm the change.

Next ops step: Camila — can your team scope the 2-day onboarding slots for the week of 12/13? Ravi — which timezone works for your engs (PST/UTC)?

Thanks — will wait to flip this into DocuSign once we align.

—Aditya
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@velocity.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-07T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal + ask: quant / batching / credit split

Ravi — quick note from leadership on the concession: we can approve the adjusted pilot credit flow with one caveat. Final offer:

- 30% upfront pilot credit (as Aditya proposed) + 15% rebate applied as a usage credit after 6 months if Velocity meets the agreed SLAs in the MAP.
- We will include the 2-day remote onboarding and a one-week tuning window at no cost.
- We can make a one-time exception to escalate the 4-bit opt variant into pilot but require an explicit A/B evaluation plan and a rollback guard.

If that is acceptable, Aditya will issue the DocuSign (https://www.docusign.com/VEL-2027-0042) and we’ll lock the onboarding dates. We aren’t able to move further on list-price discounts beyond this credit structure for pilots.

On the ops side, Camila — please draft the handoff checklist (runbook, batch params, cache config) and share by EOD 12/09.

—Lauren Bishop | Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
